agent_notes: STEPBible glosses חָשַׁק as 'he loves'; I use 'he has desired' (clung, set his heart), since the word is stronger than the usual verb of love. Cited Deut 7:7 (God desires Israel) and Deut 10:15 (the fathers). The voice shifts to the first person without a speaker formula; Ibn Ezra takes it as God speaking to the angels, Radak and Meiri as God speaking of the faithful one. The dramatic layer lets 'me' and 'my' mark the shift and adds no announcement.

agent_notes: עִמּוֹ־אָנֹכִי בְצָרָה has no verb: 'I [am] with him in trouble'. English translators supply 'will be' (KJV, ASV, Webster) or 'am' (YLT); I put 'am' in brackets in the literal layer, since the Hebrew is a nominal clause with no tense.

הַרְאֵהוּ with בְּ takes the sense 'let him look on / feast his eyes on', not 'show him my salvation' as in KJV and ASV; the preposition ב after the hiphil of ראה marks the thing seen with pleasure. STEPBible has 'on salvation my'. Whether 'my salvation' means rescue in this life, the world to come, or the days of the Messiah is disputed in the commentaries (Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri); the dramatic layer leaves the question open as the Hebrew does.

The speaker of 'I will say' is disputed. Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri and Malbim read it as a voice speaking to the addressee 'for the sake of the LORD'; Rashi has the psalmist model the confession for all. The Hebrew carries no change-of-voice marker, so I kept the first-person form and said in the commentary that the voice shifts to 'you' in v.3. Reading 'lamed' as 'of/to' rather than 'on behalf of' is the plain sense; the 'on behalf of' reading is cited from the commentators, not asserted.

agent_notes: The grammar of v.9 is notoriously difficult (who is 'you', whether 'LORD' is vocative). The MT accents (the major pause, etnachta, falls at 'my refuge') make 'You, LORD, are my refuge' one clause and 'the Most High you have made your dwelling' the second. ASV and YLT agree; KJV and Webster read 'the LORD, which is my refuge, even the Most High' as the object of 'made'. I follow the accents and flag the KJV difference. The dramatic text keeps the shift of voice, as in the Hebrew.

Стих разделён по акцентам на два обращения, как в английском; Синодальный сливает их («Ты сказал: „Господь — упование моё“; Всевышнего избрал ты прибежищем твоим»), то есть тоже делит речь на две реплики, но иначе распределяет слова.
